unmapped_findings: The as-solution-treated (pre-aging) baseline of the 19Al alloy is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV, reported once across all aging-temperature rows of Table 4; this defines the starting hardness of the sample before the 625 °C / 3 h aging.

For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high hardness is reported as 575 °C–625 °C, so this sample's 625 °C aging lies within that optimal window (with 3 h giving 863.9 ± 15.8 HV).

The temperature-dependent hardness plateau for the 19Al alloy at 625 °C aging across times is ~855–871 HV (855.6 ± 20.8 HV at 1 h, 863.9 ± 15.8 HV at 3 h, 870.7 ± 16.1 HV at 6 h, 869.5 ± 8.6 HV at 10 h), i.e. essentially time-independent at this temperature.

General conclusion (b0079): increasing the Al content slightly enhances the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn but also decreases the FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces and decreases the fracture toughness of the ultra-hard alloys, reducing the final hardening effect.

General statement (b0053): for the 19Al alloy at temperatures of 600 °C and above, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging, with numerous fine precipitates distributed within the β-Mn.
